sections.fourthRowRationale: No fourth row is used for either side; the moves separately address intelligibility, primitive concepts, conditional reduction, and motivational force.

routes.speaker: Eric Sampson
routes.position: Non-naturalist moral realism is true: some moral beliefs are stance-independently true and concern irreducible normative properties.

bridges.statement: Clear moral cases justify belief that stance-independent normative truths exist.
Stance-independent reasons are intelligible considerations favoring action regardless of an agent's goals.
Strong undefeated intuitions about paradigm cases provide prima facie justification for moral realism.
Non-natural moral facts need not satisfy empirical detection, prediction, or reductive-definition tests.
Realism explains genuine normative facts that a purely psychological account leaves out.

routes.speaker: Lance Bush
routes.position: Moral realism is unjustified or unintelligible because normativity is relational and moral-realist concepts lack independent explanatory content.

bridges.statement: There are no warranted stance-independent moral facts, and realist accounts are unintelligible, false, or trivial.
Reasons and evaluative claims are intelligible only relative to goals, standards, attitudes, or consistency relations.
Realist intuitions lack a public standard capable of adjudicating fundamental normative disagreement.
Moral-realist belief is better explained through psychological projection and culturally contingent genealogy.
Ordinary moral discourse is metaethically plural and indeterminate rather than uniformly realist.

moves.speaker: Eric Sampson
quoteEligibleExactSpans: at least some of those beliefs are true
they're true stance independently
independent of anybody's opinions or reactions
moves.attributionBasis: Eric's named opening anchor at event 28 continues uninterrupted through this definition.
moves.proposition: Moral realism combines cognitivism, non-nihilism, and the stance-independent truth of at least some moral beliefs.
moves.inventoryRationale: This opening definition fixes the pro position and the principal proposition disputed throughout the exchange.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
quoteEligibleExactSpans: I don't endorse a uniform and determinate account
a combination of meta-ethical indeterminacy and pluralism
moves.attributionBasis: Lance's named opposing opening begins at event 48 and continues through this first-person account.
moves.proposition: Ordinary moral claims lack a uniform determinate semantics and instead display metaethical indeterminacy and pluralism.
moves.inventoryRationale: This is Lance's foundational semantic position and explains why he rejects standard anti-realist classifications.

moves.speaker: Eric Sampson
quoteEligibleExactSpans: there are at least communities of people who mean the same kind of thing
at least some people are expressing beliefs
evaluate them for their truth or falsity
moves.attributionBasis: Troy explicitly directs the question to Eric at events 76–77, followed by Eric's continuous answer.

responseComponents.text: Semantic variation does not threaten realism because some communities still express shared truth-evaluable moral beliefs.

moves.proposition: Semantic diversity does not defeat cognitivism because at least some shared moral discourse expresses beliefs evaluable as true or false.
moves.inventoryRationale: This directly limits the force of Lance's pluralism without requiring uniform semantics across every speaker.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
quoteEligibleExactSpans: one implication of these empirical findings
I'm not sure that that's true
take away one of the tools in the realist kit
moves.attributionBasis: Turn-taking from Eric's answer and Lance's explicit agreement at event 97 establish the continuing Lance turn.

responseComponents.text: Even if semantic findings do not refute realism, they undermine its claimed common-sense default status.

moves.proposition: Empirical semantic uncertainty may not refute realism, but it removes the realist's common-sense burden-shifting advantage.
moves.inventoryRationale: This material qualification identifies the actual argumentative role Lance assigns to folk-semantic evidence.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
quoteEligibleExactSpans: I don't think that the two mesh
claims that are best understood as relational
independent of what I want or what I desire
moves.attributionBasis: Lance begins the invited presentation at event 284 and develops one uninterrupted first-person objection.
moves.proposition: Normativity is intelligibly relational to wants or standards, whereas stance-independent reasons do not make sense.
moves.inventoryRationale: This states the central conceptual objection underlying Lance's rejection of non-naturalist realism.

moves.speaker: Eric Sampson
quoteEligibleExactSpans: The realist comes in and says, but you do have a reason
that kid's going to drown and he matters
the cost to you would be minimal
moves.attributionBasis: The turn begins with Eric's first-person response at event 349 and continues through the drowning-child example.

responseComponents.text: The child's welfare, suffering, and the low rescue cost intelligibly favor rescue without depending on the rescuer's goals.

moves.proposition: A drowning child's welfare and the low cost of rescue provide an intelligible reason to act independently of the rescuer's goals.
moves.inventoryRationale: The example supplies Eric's concrete account of how an external reason can be understood.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
quoteEligibleExactSpans: people can say they make sense of it
they can't explain how it makes sense
there's some explanation that could be given
moves.attributionBasis: Turn-taking after Eric's example and the explicit challenge to people claiming understanding identify Lance.

responseComponents.text: Merely reporting private understanding does not publicly explain what an attitude-independent reason is.

moves.proposition: Claimed private understanding of external reasons is inadequate without a publicly communicable explanation of their meaning.
moves.inventoryRationale: This sharpens the intelligibility objection from personal incomprehension into a demand for public explanation.

moves.speaker: Eric Sampson
quoteEligibleExactSpans: the explanation was given
Because that kid matters
the reason is because he matters
moves.attributionBasis: The response follows Lance's mechanic analogy and explicitly answers its request for explanation.

responseComponents.text: The child's importance is the explanation; a hearer's failure to grasp it does not show that no explanation was supplied.

moves.proposition: The child's importance and the benefit of rescue already explain the reason, even if a particular hearer does not understand it.
moves.inventoryRationale: This is Eric's direct answer to the demand for a further public explanation.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
quoteEligibleExactSpans: some means of independently corroborating
There would be some test
I don't see any comparable standard of independent corroboration
moves.attributionBasis: Turn-taking after Eric's mechanic analogy and continuity with Lance's corroboration objection establish attribution.
moves.proposition: Unlike engineering or medicine, moral realism offers no independent test for corroborating competing accounts of what ought to be done.
moves.inventoryRationale: This introduces the epistemic objection that becomes central to the subsequent exchange.

moves.speaker: Eric Sampson
quoteEligibleExactSpans: of course we don't have one of those
these are non-natural moral facts
The fact that we don't have such a test isn't going to be that probative
moves.attributionBasis: The speaker identifies the non-naturalist position as his own and answers Lance's detector demand.

responseComponents.text: An empirical detector is not expected for non-natural facts, so its absence is not probative against them.

moves.proposition: The absence of an empirical moral-property detector is expected under non-naturalism and therefore does not count strongly against it.
moves.inventoryRationale: This is the principal realist response to the independent-corroboration demand.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
quoteEligibleExactSpans: you don't need any particular meta-ethical account
pull apart the meta-ethical considerations and the normative considerations
I'm an anti-realist. I would agree
moves.attributionBasis: The first-person declaration of anti-realism and turn-taking after Eric's appeal to agreement identify Lance.

responseComponents.text: Agreement about saving the child is compatible with anti-realism and cannot independently corroborate the realist interpretation.

moves.proposition: Shared first-order judgments do not corroborate realism because anti-realists can endorse the same actions without realist commitments.
moves.inventoryRationale: This prevents Eric's appeal to convergent judgments from functioning as distinctively metaethical evidence.

moves.speaker: Eric Sampson
quoteEligibleExactSpans: I should save this kid even if I didn't want to
justifies me in believing that there are stance-independent normative truths
I ought to do it not because of some attitude
moves.attributionBasis: The speaker explicitly describes the intended evidential role of Eric's drowning-child case.

responseComponents.text: The case is evidence because Eric himself judges rescue obligatory independently of desire, not merely because others agree.

moves.proposition: The clear intuition that one must rescue regardless of desire provides personal justification for stance-independent normative truth.
moves.inventoryRationale: This states the affirmative epistemic route from a paradigm moral case to realism.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
quoteEligibleExactSpans: that's a private appeal
not the sort of thing that can contribute very substantively to a dialectic
if realists are just appealing to this sort of evidence, it's just private evidence
moves.attributionBasis: Turn-taking after Eric's intuition defense and the first-person Bigfoot analogy identify Lance.

responseComponents.text: An intuition may privately justify its possessor yet contribute little to a shared inquiry, like an unsupported Bigfoot sighting.

moves.proposition: Realist intuition is private evidence that may justify its possessor but cannot substantively resolve the public dialectic.
moves.inventoryRationale: This directly distinguishes personal justification from evidence capable of adjudicating the debate.

moves.speaker: Eric Sampson
quoteEligibleExactSpans: it does for individuals who do have these intuitions
your intuitions are going to count as evidence for you
Whether you can convince other people is another question
moves.attributionBasis: The reply distinguishes Lance's evidence from Eric's and continues the realist first-person epistemology.

responseComponents.text: Failure to persuade others does not erase the prima facie justification that an intuition supplies to its possessor.

moves.proposition: Intuitions count as evidence for those who have them, regardless of whether that evidence persuades other people.
moves.inventoryRationale: This preserves the realist epistemic claim while conceding that justification can vary between persons.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
quoteEligibleExactSpans: suspiciously happened to accord with the cultural values
all of the same philosophical moves that moral realists can make
the same argumentative moves are available
moves.attributionBasis: Lance introduces and continuously develops the explicitly labeled Zorpian alien hypothetical.
moves.proposition: A culturally shaped alien normative system could reproduce realist argumentative moves, creating parity with claims humans regard as false.
moves.inventoryRationale: The Zorpian construction is Lance's major test of whether intuition and realist methodology can discriminate rival normative systems.

moves.speaker: Eric Sampson
quoteEligibleExactSpans: if it's true that they are moral facts
They're reasons for action that apply to you
those are what earthlings call moral facts
moves.attributionBasis: Eric conducts the preceding questions at events 639–642 and then explicitly answers the Zorpian classification.

responseComponents.text: If Zorpian requirements apply independently of attitudes, they are the same kind of normative facts realism affirms, merely relabeled.

moves.proposition: Zorpian facts stipulated as attitude-independent reasons are moral or normative facts under a different label, not a distinct parody domain.
moves.inventoryRationale: This challenges the alien comparison by denying that its purportedly separate normative category is genuinely separate.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
quoteEligibleExactSpans: I'm not going to accept that something is intelligible
it doesn't mean that it is
I don't know what it would mean
moves.attributionBasis: Troy explicitly addresses Lance at events 808–812, and Lance begins the answer at event 813.
moves.proposition: Consensus among people claiming to understand stance-independent facts does not establish that the concept is intelligible.
moves.inventoryRationale: This restates Lance's core conceptual burden after the moderator returns explicitly to the issue.

moves.speaker: Eric Sampson
quoteEligibleExactSpans: Almost everyone in metaethics does this
virtually every anti-realist says
all these anti-realists think that these people are talking perfectly good English
moves.attributionBasis: The response follows Lance's request for a definition and invokes Lance by name from the opposing position.

responseComponents.text: Widespread understanding among realists and anti-realists shifts a substantial explanatory burden onto the exceptional gibberish diagnosis.

moves.proposition: The field's broad cross-position understanding of normative language gives Lance a burden to explain why it is nevertheless gibberish.
moves.inventoryRationale: This is Eric's main dialectical response to Lance's minority intelligibility claim.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
quoteEligibleExactSpans: there's something off about the kind of realist explanations
they're not including this normative element
we can cash them out in a way where we use basically hypothetical imperatives
moves.attributionBasis: Lance explicitly corrects Eric's reconstruction beginning at event 877 and continues this distinction.

responseComponents.text: Logic differs because its practical normativity can be reduced to conditional relations between goals and methods.

moves.proposition: Logic does not vindicate primitive moral normativity because logical prescriptions can be expressed conditionally relative to an agent's aims.
moves.inventoryRationale: This answers Eric's logic analogy without treating mutual interdefinition alone as sufficient for meaninglessness.

moves.speaker: Eric Sampson
quoteEligibleExactSpans: to the extent that you can, you should change your goals
facts about what goals you ought to have
Some people just have bad goals
moves.attributionBasis: Eric announces a multi-part response at event 929 and directly answers Lance's goal-based challenge.

responseComponents.text: Normative facts do practical work by assessing and recommending revision of the goals that conditional reasoning merely takes as given.

moves.proposition: Normative facts guide action by identifying which goals agents ought to adopt or change, even when motivation initially diverges.
moves.inventoryRationale: This explains the practical role of categorical normativity rather than merely repeating that moral facts exist.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
quoteEligibleExactSpans: I am in an extreme minority position here
some argumentative burden to explain
this sort of narrow demographic, which is academic philosophers
moves.attributionBasis: Lance identifies his own minority position and proposes the empirical explanation in a continuous first-person turn.
moves.proposition: The intelligibility consensus may reflect selection into academic philosophy rather than reliable recognition of normative facts.
moves.inventoryRationale: This materially accepts the explanatory burden and states the first empirical route Lance proposes for meeting it.

moves.speaker: Eric Sampson
quoteEligibleExactSpans: Lance, as he just said, has an explanatory burden
now we just have to wait and see if it works out
if it does, then we're, the realists are going to be in trouble
moves.attributionBasis: Turn-taking after Lance's hypothesis and the third-person reference to Lance establish Eric as speaker.

responseComponents.text: The selection hypothesis could threaten realism if substantiated, but presently remains a blueprint whose success must be tested.

moves.proposition: Lance's proposed explanation could trouble realism if empirically successful, but it currently remains an unconfirmed research program.
moves.inventoryRationale: This is a material conditional concession coupled to Eric's demand that the explanatory burden actually be met.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
quoteEligibleExactSpans: need to posit the existence of moral facts
inadvertently projecting culturally acquired values onto the world
an abductive inference to the best explanation
moves.attributionBasis: Lance's alien-observer argument continues uninterrupted and explicitly describes realists in the third person.
moves.proposition: Human moral behavior and realist belief can be explained as psychological projection without positing stance-independent facts.
moves.inventoryRationale: This is Lance's explicit abductive and parsimonious case, distinct from his earlier intelligibility challenge.

moves.speaker: Eric Sampson
quoteEligibleExactSpans: what you're going to leave out is all the normative stuff
the parsimony comes in when all things are equal
all things aren't equal
moves.attributionBasis: Eric requests a follow-up at event 1310 and directly answers Lance's parsimony argument.

responseComponents.text: The accounts do not explain the same things because anti-realism omits the normative domain realism takes as part of reality.

moves.proposition: Parsimony cannot favor anti-realism when its psychological explanation leaves genuine normative facts outside its explananda.
moves.inventoryRationale: This is Eric's central response to the inference-to-the-best-explanation argument.

moves.speaker: Lance Bush
quoteEligibleExactSpans: understand the genealogy of how people came to develop
highly culturally and biologically contingent
just facts about human psychology
moves.attributionBasis: Lance explicitly distinguishes his positive anti-realist evidence at events 1537–1541 and develops this genealogy.
moves.proposition: Moral belief is plausibly a culturally and biologically contingent psychological disposition rather than detection of universal normative facts.
moves.inventoryRationale: This late constructive supplies Lance's broad positive genealogy for rejecting realism rather than merely withholding realist intuitions.

selectionAsymmetryRationale: The inventory includes twelve pro and thirteen con moves because Lance advances an additional late, source-distinct cultural-biological genealogy after Eric's last substantive reply. Retaining it avoids manufacturing symmetry and captures the con side's final positive case.
